clue.text: Those visiting Hollywood may be dazed

definitions.meaning: visitors to Hollywood hope to spot film celebrities
after a blow to the head one is stunned and sees flashing lights

explanation.surface: Tourists in Hollywood might come away bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourists in the film capital look out for celebrities, while a stunned person proverbially sees twinkling lights before the eyes.

clue.text: Charge for a pair of diamonds in auction

indicators.note: in means the two letters go inside the sale

parts.note: a sale is an auction
D abbreviates diamonds in cards, so two of them

explanation.surface: A fee for two diamonds sold at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts DD inside SALE.
explanation.definitionFit: To burden someone with a task or debt is to charge them with it.

clue.text: Bridge opponents competed and felt resentful.

parts.note: in bridge East and North sit as opponents
vied means competed

explanation.surface: Bridge players who lost the contest felt bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North-South play East-West, so East and North are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Coveting what someone else has is feeling resentment of their luck.

clue.text: Roughly three foot ahead

indicators.note: roughly suggests an approximate, rough arrangement, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: About a yard in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' rearranges THREE FOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: In front or prominent is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: Thatcher might make, a fuss

definitions.meaning: a thatcher puts the thatch up on top of a house

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher might kick up a stink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thatcher' looks like the prime minister; it is a roofer who works in straw.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofer in reed lifts the house's top, and the idiom means cheer or complain loudly.

clue.text: Picked for Korea

definitions.meaning: an old name for Korea, used under Japanese rule

explanation.surface: Selected to go to Korea.
explanation.definitionFit: Selected is a plain synonym, and the same word was the historical name of the Korean kingdom.

clue.text: Time I found a girl

parts.note: an hour is a time

explanation.surface: In time, I found a girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic belief a beautiful maiden of paradise, so a girl.

clue.text: Junior officer eats up blooming dessert

indicators.note: eats means the officer surrounds the other word

parts.note: a sub is a subaltern, a junior army officer

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: bally and blooming are both mild British swear words

explanation.surface: A young officer wolfs down a wretched pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns BALLY into YLLAB, and 'eats' puts it inside SUB. Bally and blooming are old British mild expletives.
explanation.definitionFit: A whipped cream pudding flavoured with wine, an old English sweet course.

clue.text: No repetition 'of directions? ' What rot!

indicators.note: repetition means the directions appear twice over

parts.note: N, S and E are compass directions

explanation.surface: Not giving directions twice? Rubbish!
explanation.walkthrough: 'repetition' doubles NSE after NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish or drivel; the exclamation dismisses something as absurd.

clue.text: Joint carved up -violated

indicators.note: carved up means cut into pieces and rearranged, so the letters of the next word are shuffled

explanation.surface: A joint of meat carved up and treated with violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carved up' rearranges VIOLATED. 'Joint' looks like a roast; it is the carpentry joint.
explanation.definitionFit: In carpentry a fan-shaped interlocking tenon and mortise is a classic woodworking joint.

clue.text: Bird, brown bird, slips the net

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: a bird that slips the net escapes it, so the word net leaves the bird's name

parts.note: the linnet is a small finch

explanation.surface: A brown bird escapes the netting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slips the' removes NET from LINNET, leaving LIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wading sandpiper of shores and mudflats, so a bird.

clue.text: Nearly 500 wearing hair shirts

parts.note: nigh means nearly

indicators.note: the hair is wearing the numeral, so it surrounds it

parts.note: tresses are long locks of hair
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Almost five hundred people in hair shirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts D inside TRESSES. 'hair shirts' looks like the penitent's garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Women's night garments are loose shirts worn in bed.

clue.text: The subject of a false 'story, for instance, that's put about

parts.note: a lie is a false story

indicators.note: put about means turned round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates for example, for instance

explanation.surface: A rumour that is spread about is the subject of a false story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's put about' turns EG round to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal terms the word names a vassal owing allegiance, a subject of the lord.

clue.text: Get rid of the bird in 5

indicators.note: in means the bird's name goes inside the other word

parts.note: the answer to 5 across means picked or select, so elite
the mina is a variant spelling of the myna, a starling

explanation.surface: Remove the bird found in the fifth clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' points to 5 across, whose meaning 'picked' gives ELITE; 'in' puts MINA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove or do away with something entirely is a synonym for getting rid of it.

clue.text: Be mother for party, with some of the Royals, for' instance

parts.note: a do is a party
in card games the king, queen and jack, the royal court cards, are among the honours

explanation.surface: Pour the tea at a party attended by some members of the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'be mother' is British slang for pouring the tea. In card games the honours are the top cards, among them the royal court cards, which is the sense 'some of the Royals' points at.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means acting as host and serving, as the person pouring tea at a gathering does.

clue.text: Child-minder heartlessly attacked — she was a kid herself once

definitions.text: she was a kid herself once

parts.note: a nanny looks after children

indicators.note: heartlessly means the central letter is taken out

parts.note: got at means attacked or got at someone

explanation.surface: A nanny was brutally assaulted, though she was once a child herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' removes the middle T of GOT AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A female of the species was once a young one, which is what a kid is.

clue.text: Densely planted trees round the entrance to Stonehenge

indicators.note: round means the trees surround the letter

parts.note: a thicket is a dense group of trees

indicators.note: the entrance to means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Thick trees grow round the way into Stonehenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts S, the first letter of Stonehenge, inside THICKET.
explanation.definitionFit: Closely packed or set thick, as with trees in a copse.

clue.text: First view from, say, North East

parts.note: Lord North was a prime minister, an example of a premier

explanation.surface: An initial glimpse from the north-east of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North' looks like the compass point; it is Lord North, British prime minister 1770-82, and 'say' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening public performance of a film or play is its first showing.

clue.text: The ring-road's rerouted by negotiation

indicators.note: traffic rerouted takes a different path, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the S comes from the contraction of is

explanation.surface: The ring road has been diverted following negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rerouted' rearranges THE RING-ROAD'S, where 's stands for 'is' and supplies an S.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard bargaining with shrewd give and take is the idiomatic sense of the phrase.

clue.text: -This line was her undoing

indicators.note: undoing means taking apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rope that caused a woman's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undoing' rearranges WAS HER.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick cable or rope used for mooring or towing a ship.

clue.text: In hospital, I can't type

indicators.note: in means the letters are found within the words

explanation.surface: A patient in hospital says they cannot type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the run spanning hospITAL I Can't.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping print is a typeface style.

clue.text: Officer holding gold in a cupboard

indicators.note: in means the heraldic gold sits inside the piece of furniture

parts.note: a commode is a chest of drawers or small cabinet
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: An officer keeps his gold hidden in a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts OR inside COMMODE.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval rank above captain, so a commissioned officer.

clue.text: Battle site has no water for an aquatic creature.

indicators.note: has no means the stream is taken away from the site's name

parts.note: Otterburn in Northumberland was the site of a battle in 1388
a burn is a Scottish stream

explanation.surface: A battlefield without water is no place for a river animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Otterburn is a battle site in Northumberland, England; a burn is a Scottish and northern English word for a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish-eating mammal living in rivers is an aquatic creature.

clue.text: Indeed, a good man should get a rise

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes, indeed
St, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A virtuous man deserves a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the ingredient is what makes dough rise, so it 'should get a rise' out of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: The fungus used in baking produces gas that makes dough swell upward.

clue.text: Bloodhound almost killed run-away girl

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite finished, its last letter dropped

parts.note: slew is the past tense of slay, killed

indicators.note: away means the run letter goes off from the name

parts.note: Ruth is a girl's name
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A tracker dog nearly caught and killed a girl who had run away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SLEW to SLE; 'away' takes R out of RUTH, leaving UTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleuth-hound was the old name for a bloodhound, a dog that tracks by scent.

clue.text: Backing from displaced Poles outside the country

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters surround the country
displaced means moved out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the country is the USA

explanation.surface: Support from Polish emigrants living abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displaced' turns POLES into ESPOL, and 'outside' wraps it round USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking up or supporting a cause is a formal sense of the word, as well as betrothal.

clue.text: Those who are not officers they are outside, in view

indicators.note: are outside means the word they surrounds the other ranks

parts.note: taken as written
ORs, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Ordinary soldiers are kept outside while things are in view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are outside' puts OR (other ranks, the non-officers) inside THEY.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion or idea held about something is a sense shared with a view.

clue.text: Coteries fashioned for the enlightened minority

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Exclusive cliques formed for an enlightened few.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashioned' rearranges COTERIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Understood only by a select inner circle of initiates.
